method: Primary publisher/author documentation and versioned research, with relevant sections inspected; original examples labeled separately. No benchmark statistics or imported source text.

claims.versionContext: Version 3, 26 May 2023; ACL 2023. Section 2 separates devising a plan from carrying it out in reasoning prompts; its experiments are not production-agent trials.
claims.supports: Planning followed by execution in prompted reasoning
claims.limits: Reasoning benchmarks and historical models; not deployed-agent reliability

claims.versionContext: Version 2, 3 December 2023; NeurIPS 2023. Sections 3–4 describe candidate generation, evaluation and search in selected problem-solving tasks.
claims.sectionsChecked: Sections 3–4; candidate generation/evaluation and BFS/DFS search
claims.supports: Exploration and backtracking over intermediate candidate thoughts
claims.limits: Selected puzzle/writing tasks; model self-evaluation is not independent proof

claims.versionContext: Version 3, 10 March 2023; section 2 describes reasoning interleaved with actions and observations. Results concern the evaluated environments and models.
claims.supports: Feedback informs subsequent reasoning and actions
claims.limits: Selected models and environments; no universally trustworthy observations

claims.versionContext: Living implementation documentation checked 17 October 2026; checkpointing, resumption and Idempotency sections distinguish saved task results from unfinished tasks that may run again.
claims.supports: Saved completed task results versus unfinished tasks that may execute again
claims.limits: Checkpointing does not guarantee every external effect occurs exactly once

claims.versionContext: Living implementation documentation checked 17 October 2026; How Workflow replay works and Resuming a Workflow describe event history and replay constraints in Temporal.
claims.sectionsChecked: How Workflow replay works; Resuming a Workflow
claims.supports: Event-history replay, deterministic decisions and recorded activity results
claims.limits: Workflow replay is distinct from activity retries and end-to-end effects

claims.versionContext: Primary engineering guidance checked 17 October 2026; request identifiers, semantic equivalence, late requests and changed intent. An API-specific contract is needed; this is not a universal exactly-once guarantee.
claims.sectionsChecked: Retrying and side effects; client request identifiers; semantic equivalence; late requests; different intent
claims.supports: Unknown responses, request identity and API-specific deduplication contracts
claims.limits: No universal or unlimited exactly-once guarantee

claims.versionContext: Versioned 25 November 2025 specification, checked 17 October 2026; HTTP authorization roles, resource parameters, scope and access-token validation. It does not define every application permission.
claims.sectionsChecked: Purpose and Scope; Roles; Resource Parameter; Token Handling; scope selection
claims.supports: HTTP authorization roles, resource audience and receiver token validation
claims.limits: Transport/version-specific; not every application permission or action-specific consent

claims.versionContext: February 2020 Standards Track RFC; sections 2–3 distinguish the intended resource from scope and explain audience restrictions. Describes an OAuth mechanism, not agent behavior or user approval of individual actions.
claims.sectionsChecked: Sections 2 and 3; scope/resource distinction and audience restrictions
claims.supports: Requested resource and access scope differ; intended audience and tenant boundary
claims.limits: OAuth mechanism is not proof of the user intent for an agent action

claims.versionContext: Versioned security guidance checked 17 October 2026; token passthrough and confused-deputy risks. These requirements do not prove that a particular deployment enforces them.
claims.supports: Delegated authority must not become unrestricted downstream access
claims.limits: Requirements do not establish compliance by a particular deployment

claims.versionContext: Living project documentation checked 17 October 2026; Sentry and Gofer describe an application-kernel isolation design and compatibility boundaries.
claims.supports: Application-kernel boundary, mediated files and compatibility limits
claims.limits: One implementation; no equivalence among all sandbox products

claims.versionContext: Living security design documentation checked 17 October 2026; goals, host interactions, resource controls and hardware-side-channel limitations. No blanket sandbox or virtual-machine ranking follows.
claims.sectionsChecked: Goals; Other Vectors; host controls; hardware-side-channel limits
claims.supports: System interface exposure, resource/network controls and residual risks
claims.limits: Sandbox is not a substitute for secure architecture; no blanket security ranking

claims.versionContext: Engineering announcement published 20 October 2025, checked 17 October 2026; filesystem/network isolation in that product’s described runtime. Vendor-reported statistics and present product defaults are not reproduced here.
claims.sectionsChecked: Sandboxed bash tool; filesystem/network restrictions and subprocess coverage
claims.supports: Described runtime separates filesystem and network isolation
claims.limits: Historical vendor description; omit internal statistics and current-default claims

claims.versionContext: Living project documentation checked 17 October 2026; instrumentation, signals, metrics, logs and distributed tracing. Describes software telemetry, not an agent factual-accuracy measure.
claims.sectionsChecked: What is Observability; Reliability and metrics; Understanding distributed tracing
claims.supports: Instrumentation, logs, traces and numeric aggregation answer different questions
claims.limits: Operational telemetry does not establish agent factual correctness

claims.versionContext: Living project documentation checked 17 October 2026; trace/span identifiers, parent relationships, timing, attributes and status. Instrumented status reflects the operation being tracked.
claims.sectionsChecked: Root/child span examples; trace and span identifiers; attributes/status
claims.supports: Operation timing and linkage form a trace with defined scope
claims.limits: Operation status is not task-level or factual success

claims.versionContext: Living Python SDK documentation checked 17 October 2026; agent/tool/handoff spans, sensitive-data controls and export/redaction behavior. SDK-specific behavior is not enabled or installed by this article.
claims.sectionsChecked: Traces and spans; Sensitive data; Custom tracing processors; Redaction before export
claims.supports: Agent/tool tracing, potentially sensitive inputs/outputs and export/redaction boundaries
claims.limits: SDK-specific; no instrumentation installed or export enabled here

claims.versionContext: Primary research publication and linked camera-ready paper, checked 17 October 2026; Linked-paper guideline discussion address capabilities, dismissal, correction and controls. Design evaluation is not proof that human review prevents every error.
claims.sectionsChecked: Linked CHI 2019 camera-ready paper, guideline discussion and correction/dismissal examples
claims.supports: Communicating capabilities, supporting dismissal/correction and user controls
claims.limits: Design-guideline evaluation; not a guarantee of effective review or correctness

claims.versionContext: Living implementation documentation checked 17 October 2026; pausing, resuming with external input, thread identity and re-execution rules. An interrupt mechanism is not a complete reviewer-authentication or authorization policy.
claims.sectionsChecked: Pausing/resuming; same thread identity; Rules of interrupts; node re-execution
claims.supports: External resume input and repeated pre-interrupt node code
claims.limits: Mechanism does not authenticate a reviewer or establish approval scope

claims.versionContext: Versioned 25 November 2025 specification, checked 17 October 2026; User Interaction Model recommends human ability to deny invocations and visible tool/confirmation UI. Protocol guidance is distinct from this project’s article-publication policy.
claims.supports: Recommended deny ability, visible invocations and confirmations
claims.limits: Attributed protocol recommendation, distinct from project article-publication policy
